title: Small Losses, Major Losses and the Basis the Host's Share Is Measured On
content:
The size of the money the plan accepted on a claim under the Keyturn Host Protection Plan settles the basis the host's share is measured on. The marketplace's small-loss mark is 3500 and its major-loss mark is 25000.

- Where the money the plan accepted on the claim is below the marketplace's small-loss mark, the share is measured as the marketplace's small-loss proportion, 40 percent, of the money accepted.
- Where the money accepted reaches the marketplace's major-loss mark, it is measured as the deductible the plan publishes together with the marketplace's major-loss proportion, 5 percent, of the money accepted above that mark.
- Where the money accepted lies between the two marks, it is measured at the deductible the plan publishes.

### Worked readings (hypothetical figures, on a published deductible of 1500)

| Money accepted on the claim | Basis | Share measured at |
|---|---|---|
| 2000 | 40 percent of the money accepted | 800.00 |
| 3500 | the published deductible | 1500.00 |
| 10000 | the published deductible | 1500.00 |
| 25000 | the deductible with 5 percent of nothing above the mark | 1500.00 |
| 41000 | the deductible with 5 percent of 16000 | 2300.00 |

Money accepted of exactly 3500 is not below the small-loss mark, so the deductible basis governs; money accepted of exactly 25000 reaches the major-loss mark, and the proportion is taken on the part above it, which at that figure is nothing.

### What the records show

The money accepted is what the appraisal standing on the claim booked as owed to the host on this enrolment.
